newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel CPI-linked bonds higher on scarce supply.
newsitem.headline: Israel CPI-linked bonds higher on scarce supply.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Sunday with prices of CPI-linked bonds rising on expectations of a tight supply in August, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.21 pct to 110.79
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.24 pct to 110.98
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.12 pct 110.1
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.01 pct to 110.82
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.14 pct to 108.43
Volume including Makams was a low 129 million shekels.

"The trend in the market is very clear. Yields on CPI-linked bonds are on their way down because of the tight supply of these bonds. Yields of unlinked bonds will hold stable until publication of July's consumer price index (CPI)," said Ilan Doron of Solid Financial Markets.
Doron said that prices of CPI-linked bonds had risen on Sunday on expectations that in August there would be a tight supply of bonds in general and CPI-linked bonds in particular.

"Government bond redemptions are expected to total 4.1 billion shekels in August against issues of 1.4 billion shekels," Doron said. "Fears of a rise in inflation is one of the reasons CPI-linked bond prices are up, but the main reason is that traders are afraid of a shortage in these bonds."
Yields of CPI-linked bonds ranged between 3.7 percent to 4.0 percent. Doron predicted yields of CPI-long bonds, now around 3.8 percent, would be around 3.7 percent by the end of the year.
Prices of unlinked bonds rose on Sunday but yields remained stable. Doron said demand for unlinked bonds was up despite fears of a higher inflation.
"The market fears a rise in inflation and that is why yields of unlinked bonds are stable and will continue to be so at least until July's CPI is published," Doron said.

"At the same time, some traders are buying these bonds because even if inflation will be higher in the coming months, inflation expectations for the next 12 months are around 8.5 percent. Inflation may be higher but it will certainly not boom," Doron said.
Yields of one-year unlinked bonds were around 13 percent, he said.

The rise of the dollar against the shekel in June, which caused June's CPI to rise a steep 1.1 percent, has triggered fears of a series of high indices in July and August. The shekel has recovered some of its losses against the dollar in the past two weeks.
July's CPI will be published on August 15.
"The atmosphere in the market is positive and investors are looking forward with a positive attitude," said a trader at a major institutional investor.
Dollar-linked bonds traded stable, the trader said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.54 shekels)
